result.lens: disk guard (A124): guard008 batch-admission bound, launcher009 per-start bound, binder007 inheritance, G7-SCOPE-1 inventory coverage
result.verdict: PASS: 0 blocking under A115, with 8 NOTEs. guard008 enforces sum(declared output_cap_bytes) + 20 GiB on the declared volume at batch admission. That sum equals calls x cap when caps are uniform. The check is validate's default disk_batch=True, which runs in launcher009 main() for both the root and --worker invocations, and also in binder007 at bind time. launcher009 enforces one cap + 20 GiB twice per start: beside memory_free at L120, and again just before Popen at L127. Free space is statvfs f_bavail x f_frsize, which equals df, in GiB. The diffs show nothing else changed. An honest HEADLINE11-shaped batch (11 x 96 GiB) was admitted and every call started at the exact bound. On the real volume, External1 has 3273.2 GiB free against a 1076 GiB bound. No honest call is wrongly refused, wrongly admitted or mis-recorded. Every NOTE is about procedure, custody or test labelling.

findings.title: Disk refusals are recorded under a generic reason, with no case name and no df reading
findings.evidence: W6 and W7 ran the actual launcher009.worker on scratch copies. A per-start DISK_START_BOUND drains the batch under reason WORKER_INTERRUPTED_OR_ERROR with case null. The free/required dict returned at L120 (disk=G.disk_admission(plan,pending[0])) is never used, and validate() discards the batch reading, so no df reading is kept at admission or at any start. When the L127 pre-Popen recheck refuses, the log already holds step4_admission_decision admitted:true for a case that never started (W7: SYNTH0 admitted:true, 0 monitors, finished []). A batch refusal in the worker's own main() leaves only a traceback in launcher_log (W3). Entries for completed calls stay correct (W6: SYNTH0 and SYNTH1 passed True). This is a custody gap, not a physics mis-record. A successor could name the case, use the DISK_* code as the reason and log free/required. Until then, root records a df reading at admission, as the D17 interim said.
findings.label: TESTED

findings.title: Darwin statvfs block counts are 32-bit: exact below 16 TiB free, and overflow can only under-report
findings.evidence: The SDK's sys/_types.h has 'typedef unsigned int __darwin_fsblkcnt_t', used by statvfs. Wrapping was observed: External1 f_ffree 4257235968 = df ifree 34322007040 mod 2^32. External1 has f_blocks 976703436 < 2^32 (3.73 TiB), so f_bavail x f_frsize = 858050176 x 4096 = 3273.202 GiB, exactly df -k Available. The internal volume reads 396.291 GiB both ways (B14a). Wrapping can only under-report, which fails closed. On APFS f_bsize is 1 MiB and would over-report 256x; the code correctly uses f_frsize (B1). f_bavail equals f_bfree on both volumes.
findings.label: TESTED

findings.title: Bytes written outside the declared caps come out of the 20 GiB reserve
findings.evidence: The monitor (ba031c23) caps only dir_bytes(outdir): apparent st_size, polled every 2 s. The receipt, .launch.json, .stdout.txt/.stderr.txt (driver output, uncapped), monitor_log and launcher_log all sit outside output_cap_bytes. When admission is at the exact bound and each call writes its full cap, the last start has zero slack: the W4 slack list ends 0, 0, and the chain's minimum free was 116 GiB = 96 + 20. These extra files could therefore trip DISK_START_BOUND only if free space at admission were within a few such bytes of the bound. The real margin is 3273.2 GiB free against 1076 GiB for HEADLINE11 at 96 GiB caps. It fails closed.
findings.label: TESTED

findings.title: Bound semantics: sum of caps, one cap per start, other External1 writers, volume identity
findings.evidence: (1) sum(caps) + 20 GiB equals calls x cap when caps are uniform. The 96 GiB cap recommended in S4-R-D8 is uniform; I found no ruling on it in the posts I read. With mixed caps the guard uses the exact sum, not calls x max. (2) The per-start bound reserves only the next call's cap. The remaining output of calls already running is covered by the batch bound only if nothing else writes to External1. core_priority attests that the campaign and step 2 are inactive, but not other lanes' External1 moves; CURRENT_INSTRUCTIONS lists .git (350 GiB) and 289 GiB of dark-sector files as pending. (3) Later direct batches will be refused, by design, if the campaign (3.25 TiB on the typical model) fills External1; this falls to root's D3 retention ruling. (4) Volume identity is the mount path /Volumes/External1 plus st_dev equality. There is no VolumeUUID pin, but an impostor volume would also need the run root on it.
findings.label: FORMAL

result.verdict: PASS, 0 blocking under A115. Both PRELAUNCH v001 (c821121f) and v002 (403d642b) call guard007's native_preflight(admission, call) unchanged, under guard007's own fence, which is nested inside the native's internal fence. findings.title: The PRELAUNCH run's interpreter and flags are not pinned; running without -B (or without -I) can refuse an honest call
findings.evidence: INTERFACE_V001 and INTERFACE_V002 give only the CLI arguments. Under guard007's fence, the first import of an uncached module makes Python try to write a .pyc, and the fence refuses that write. TESTED on copies: an unmanaged import passes under -I -B and is refused with PREFLIGHT_WRITE_REFUSED under -I -X pycache_prefix=<scratch> without -B, leaving no outputs (MY_RESULTS_nob_B/nob_noB.json). Without -I, PYTHONPATH or user site-packages could change which numpy the tail library loads compared with the launcher's -I -B run, which would only fail the launch replay closed (FORMAL). Exposure is low: the pinned runtime ships stdlib and numpy caches, and native sources are compiled from verified bytes and never cached. Fix: document the invocation as <launcher PYTHON> -I -B step4_prelaunch_cx1v002.py ..., the same interpreter and flags as binder007 and launcher009.

corrections: Correction (precision, NOTE): L120's per-start check runs on every 60 s poll while calls are pending and the worker is not draining. That includes polls where the memory gate or ramp logs admitted:false, so it is not only 'twice per start'. A below-bound reading on a waiting poll drains the rest of the batch. Re-derived on scratch copies (R1: 11 x 96 GiB, starting free exactly 1076 GiB, calls writing gradually up to their caps, 5 gated polls): all 11 started, rc 0, minimum free 116 GiB. The finding that no honest call is wrongly refused stands.

Correction (arithmetic, N6): f_blocks 976703436 x 4096 B = 4,000,577,273,856 B, which is 3.64 TiB (diskutil reports 4.0 TB), not 3.73 TiB. It is still far below the 16 TiB point where the 32-bit count wraps. Re-observed: f_bavail x f_frsize = 858050176 x 4096 = 3514573520896 B, which equals df -k Available x 1024 = 3273.2017 GiB. f_ffree 4257235968 = 34322007040 mod 2^32. The SDK's sys/_types.h L70 has 'typedef unsigned int __darwin_fsblkcnt_t'.

Correction (attribution, N8(3)): D17's 3.25 TiB typical (8.73 TiB worst) covers all step-4 calls, of which the 33 direct calls are about 709.5 GiB. It is not the campaign alone. Supporting arithmetic: with no other External1 writer, even full 96 GiB outputs let HEADLINE11, DIII4, SENS_LO9 and SENS_HI9 clear their bounds in sequence (SENS_HI9 needs 884 GiB with about 969 GiB left of 3273.2). So refusing an honest direct batch takes an extra writer: a campaign wave, the storage moves, or the POST_S1 batch, whose size is not yet registered. That agrees with N8(2)/(3).
